page: Microsoft Azure E32as_v6 is an Eav6-family virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 25%. Multi-threaded performance is also notable, with Geekbench multi-core and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving strong ratings. Memory subsystem performance is highlighted by a strong PassMark memory score, though raw memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks fall within the average range. Cryptographic capabilities are strong, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions.

Given its memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8, the E32as_v6 is structured for memory-intensive workloads. It demonstrates strong capabilities in text and image processing, as well as low-latency small-model LLM inference. However, database operations and multi-core stress-ng benchmarks remain in the average tier. The absence of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which represents a qualitative tradeoff in I/O-heavy scenarios. This instance is suited for memory-optimized applications, enterprise relational databases, and data-processing pipelines that do not require local NVMe drives.
description: The Microsoft Azure E32as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, this instance provides an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio but lacks bundled local storage and GPUs. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU execution, high-tier Geekbench multi-core scores, and strong memory performance, while multi-core stress-ng and database operations perform in the average range. The server supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration. It is suited for memory-intensive workloads, enterprise applications, and data processing tasks that rely on external Premium Storage.
